Dragging its long abdomen behind it in the dew of the dawn grass, the arachnid searches for a fresh bloom of flowers to prepare 
for the rising sun. Once settled among the grass and stalks, it will raise its back to the sky. Expanding the segments of its pygidium 
into a semblance of the flowers that surround it, the scorpithine then quickly migrates pigment cells within to match the color of the 
surrounding petals and masterfully camouflages itself in the underbrush. Patiently it will wait with an eerie stillness in the warm 
morning sun until an unwary pollinator will chance upon its false blossom. Unlike the flowers around it, its petals are lined with 
gripping serrated edges, ready to close in on the prey. And once they do, the long clawed hind legs repeatably stab the struggling prey 
until it ceases to move and the arachnid is then ready to feast.

False Flower While the scorpithine remains motionless, it is 
indistinguishable from nearby flowers. A creature within 5 ft. 
of the scorpithine can make a DC 12 Wisdom (Perception) check 
to discern if the flower is real or false. If a Creature touches the 
scorpithine, it can make one Numbing Tarsus Attack against that 
Creature as a Reaction.
